fault_name: Excessive Lumbar Arching in Overhead Press
biomechanical_root_cause: Leaning backward significantly to recruit upper pectorals to assist the deltoids. Occurs when anterior core (rectus abdominis) or gluteus maximus fail to maintain a neutral pelvic tilt under overhead load.
verbal_cues: Squeeze your glutes rock-hard and pull your ribcage down toward your belt.
Push your head through the window once the bar clears your forehead.
Press the weight up, not yourself back.

corrective_drills.coaching_points: Half-kneeling position prevents lumbar hyperextension by forcing hip extension on the down knee.
Strengthens the anterior core against axial extension forces.

biomechanical_root_cause: Triceps fatigue or restricted glenohumeral upward rotation preventing full terminal elbow extension.
verbal_cues: Press the ceiling through the roof at the top.
Shrug your shoulders slightly upward at full extension to lock the joint.

corrective_drills.drill: Overhead Pin Presses from Forehead Height
corrective_drills.coaching_points: Overloads the lockout portion of the press to build triceps power and lockout confidence.
